title: Mystery #1: The Case of the Missing Diamond
description: Detective, we need your help with The Case of the Missing Diamond. This is an easy investigation requiring you to use Basic SELECT. Retrieve the list of suspects from the registry. Clue #1.
lesson: Basic SELECT statements are the foundation of any investigation. Use SELECT * to gather all available intelligence on a subject.
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE suspects (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, alibi VARCHAR); INSERT INTO suspects VALUES (1, 'Prof. Moriarty', 'At the university'), (2, 'Irene Adler', 'Opera rehearsal'), (3, 'Col. Moran', 'Playing cards');
expected_query: SELECT * FROM suspects;

solutions.query: SELECT * FROM suspects;
solutions.description: The most straightforward way to list everyone.

hint: Analyze the schema carefully before making your deduction. Expected output columns: id, name, alibi. Use 'AS <name>' to alias columns.

title: Mystery #2: The Cipher in the Shadows
description: Detective, we need your help with The Cipher in the Shadows. This is an medium investigation requiring you to use Filtering. We need to find suspects who have an alibi related to the opera. Clue #2.
lesson: Filtering with WHERE clauses lets you narrow down your list of suspects based on specific clues.
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE suspects (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, alibi VARCHAR); INSERT INTO suspects VALUES (1, 'Prof. Moriarty', 'At the university'), (2, 'Irene Adler', 'Opera rehearsal'), (3, 'Col. Moran', 'Playing cards');
expected_query: SELECT name FROM suspects WHERE alibi LIKE '%Opera%';

solutions.query: SELECT name FROM suspects WHERE alibi LIKE '%Opera%';

title: Mystery #4: The Midnight Train Mystery
description: Detective, we need your help with The Midnight Train Mystery. This is an easy investigation requiring you to use Joins. Connect the suspects to the locations they were seen at. Clue #4.

title: Mystery #5: The Secret of the Old Manor
description: Detective, we need your help with The Secret of the Old Manor. This is an medium investigation requiring you to use Subqueries. Identify suspects who were seen at locations where a crime occurred. Clue #5.
lesson: Subqueries allow you to nest investigations within investigations. Sometimes, though, joining the evidence directly is faster.

expected_query: SELECT name FROM suspects WHERE id IN (SELECT suspect_id FROM sightings WHERE location IN (SELECT location FROM crimes));

solutions.query: SELECT DISTINCT s.name FROM suspects s JOIN sightings si ON s.id = si.suspect_id JOIN crimes c ON si.location = c.location;
solutions.description: Joins are often faster than nested subqueries for this type of operation.

solutions.query: SELECT name FROM suspects WHERE id IN (SELECT suspect_id FROM sightings WHERE location IN (SELECT location FROM crimes));
solutions.description: Nested subqueries, logical but can be slower on large datasets.

hint: Analyze the schema carefully before making your deduction. Expected output columns: name. Use 'AS <name>' to alias columns.
